title: Yash Highvoltage Ltd - 544310 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 57% to INR235.1 crore with EBITDA margin of 25.7%; order book above INR400 crore and FY27 order-booking target of INR500+ crore.
summary.overview: Yash Highvoltage reported record FY26 revenue of INR235.1 crore (up 57%), EBITDA of INR60.4 crore (up 75%, 25.7% margin, about 260 bps higher) and PAT of INR37.4 crore (15.9% margin). H2 FY26 revenue was INR135.5 crore (up 46% YoY), with H2 EBITDA of INR37.2 crore and PAT of INR23.7 crore. Order book stood at over INR400 crore on 31 March 2026. Management said the Greenfield RIP facility is in final commissioning, with trial production by end Q2 FY27 and commercial production targeted around October 2026.

segments.name: OIP bushings
segments.commentary: Roughly half of FY26 volumes (about 3,500-3,600 units out of about 7,200); management says OIP is in shortage and deliveries are constrained by capacity, with a brownfield expansion planned.

segments.name: RIP bushings
segments.commentary: Roughly half of FY26 volumes (about 3,500-3,600 units); core is still imported (about 95% per the presentation), and localisation via the Greenfield facility at Jarod is targeted in H2 FY27.

segments.name: HCP / high current
segments.commentary: Balance of volumes in FY26 (combined with OIP, about 15-18% of order book per management).

segments.name: Retrofit
segments.commentary: About 6-7% of overall revenue per management; described as high-margin, with no segment EBITDA disclosed.

segments.name: Sukrut Electric (acquired)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR25-26 crore; management targets INR150-160 crore in 4-5 years (5-6x growth). No Sukrut EBITDA guidance given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 invoicing target of INR360-400 crore (management: 40-45% growth).
Order inflow target of at least INR500 crore in FY27.
EBITDA margin to be maintained around 24-25% in FY27; margin expansion expected from FY28 as import dependence falls.
Long-term growth aspiration of around 40-42% for the next four to five years.
Exports to reach at least 20% of revenue in the next two to three years.
Greenfield RIP facility: trial production by end Q2 FY27, commercial RIP core production about 3-4 months after internal trials and type tests; management targets October 2026.
Total capacity to rise to about 15,000 bushings (about INR700 crore revenue potential), with about INR100 crore for OIP and the balance for RIP.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 9,000-10,000 bushings; about 7,000+ produced in FY26 (75-80% utilisation); FY27 utilisation target 65-70%.
Greenfield facility at Jarod (about 20 km from Baroda airport): design expanded from 220 kV to 550 kV; adds about 5,000-7,000 units a year, focused on RIP/RIS.
Greenfield capex of about INR153 crore, of which about INR80 crore spent; balance expected within two to three months.
Equity raise approval up to INR150 crore; management is eyeing INR100-110 crore for capex (550 kV production, testing, brownfield) and working capital of INR28-30 crore.
Constraints in autoclave capacity; new autoclaves being invested in. Brownfield OIP expansion planned to address OIP shortage.
demand_pricing: Management says demand exceeds global bushing supply; transformer OEMs are giving blanket orders for 24-36 months.
Prices are secured with suppliers and customers via pass-through arrangements for commodity and currency moves; management says indirect cost escalation from oil/gas is being passed on.
Management sees no direct impact from the Middle East war; no exports to or imports from affected countries.
Management says Chinese bushings have never been restricted in India, yet Indian buyers have not bought them, citing pricing, availability and service.
Competitive RIP entrants in India named as CG Power, Hitachi India and MIM (Massa Izolyator Mehru).

qa_highlights.question: Top-line growth expected over the next 2-3 years and impact of the Middle East war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 40-42% growth for the next four to five years (38-40% CAGR over the past five to six years); no direct war impact, only indirect cost escalation passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new RIP plant contribute revenue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production by end Q2 FY27; job-work assembly and testing revenue starts earlier, with indigenous RIP commercial revenue expected towards year-end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross and EBITDA margins improve in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonally higher H2 volumes, scale-driven negotiation, customer price recovery, supplier price negotiation and currency hedging; no single specific reason.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of margin compression if lower-kV capacity comes online across the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to hold given rising global demand, localisation of RIP cores and export pricing for RIP, and sees input-stage margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sukrut revenue potential and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukrut revenue about INR25-26 crore in FY26, targeted at INR150-160 crore in 4-5 years; management declined to give Sukrut EBITDA guidance until later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total capacity after expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15,000 bushings with a revenue potential of close to INR700 crore; about INR100 crore OIP and the balance RIP.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity rather than debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is mathematically cheaper but it wants good investors on the cap table and prefers to remain debt-free.

qa_highlights.question: Cyber incident impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No recovery to date; a police complaint has been filed and the expense has already been charged to the P&L.

risks_watch: Commissioning and type-test success for the Greenfield RIP core line; management says a 2-3 month delay would not affect FY27 guidance.
Input-cost and currency volatility from oil, gas, insulators and rupee depreciation; Middle East war effects over the next two to three months.
Supply-chain bottlenecks: vendor development takes about 6 months and suppliers may deprioritise the company; people attrition in a niche skill set.
Pricing and capacity risk if sub-400 kV capacity expands industry-wide, or if restrictions on Chinese bushings are eased.
Sukrut integration and profitability not yet disclosed; equity raise size (INR100-110 crore vs INR150 crore approval) still to be finalised.
Swiss technology contract for core knowledge runs to mid-2027 for supplies; the agreement itself has ended.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, growth and order visibility, but measured and somewhat hedged on timelines and specifics. Management declined to give several numbers (RIP/OIP realisations, retrofit EBITDA, Sukrut EBITDA) and kept some answers general.

So, we, we have a target to book at least INR500 plus crores order this year also.
Sukrut, we assume that in next four to five years, we should be able to cross at least INR150 to INR160 crores of revenue.

adds.what: Greenfield RIP facility at Jarod, design expanded to 550 kV, adds about 5,000-7,000 bushings a year (RIP/RIS focus)
Brownfield OIP expansion (capacity to reach about 15,000 total bushings, about INR100 crore for OIP)

growth.why: FY27 invoicing guided at INR360-400 crore (40-45% growth) with order book above INR400 crore and inflow target of INR500+ crore; Greenfield Jarod facility trial by end Q2 FY27 and commercial production targeted October 2026, but capacity additions are only partly funded (INR80 of INR153 crore spent) and the OIP brownfield is unscheduled.
